title: How To Get Parents On Your Side
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin identifies one strategy he claims outperforms all other parent-relations tactics combined: giving students a genuinely great first day, first week, and first month of school. He argues that this single lever requires no extra effort and no change to the teacher's program, yet delivers exactly what parents want—an inspired, motivated, engaged child. The article contrasts parents dreading a bad report with parents relieved and thrilled when their child comes home excited, noting that such relief translates directly into word-of-mouth praise to other parents and to the principal. He frames the strategy as preventive: happy students upfront eliminate the need for damage control later, replacing complaints and after-school confrontations with parents who volunteer and ask how they can help.
points: A genuinely great first day, week, and month of school is, by itself, the most powerful parent-relations strategy available.
This strategy requires no extra work and no change to a teacher's existing program or personal style.
Parents primarily want their child inspired, excited, and engaged—not any particular teaching method.
A child's enthusiastic report at home turns into unsolicited praise passed on to other parents and to the principal.
Investing in a strong start prevents the need for later damage control, replacing complaints with parent volunteers and goodwill.
quotes: Which is why it’s critical that you get them on your side, critical that they like you and trust you and support your program.
It’s so powerful, in fact, that it outperforms all other strategies combined.
You make sure your students have a great first day—as well as first week and first month—of school .
Because they know that when their child is happy, they learn. They grow socially and academically.
So when their child leaps into their car smiling from ear to ear and offering a glowing review of their first day or first week, they exhale a summer’s worth of tension.
So instead of having parents in your ear , waiting for you after school, and emailing you in the middle of the night, they merely smile and wave.
